At 9:14, I saw the northbound train strike the shopping cart and stop halfway across Pine Street. The driver stayed in the cab. A woman in a green coat pulled the cart free before the police arrived.

“It left an indelible mark on the neighborhood,” the mayor said that afternoon. The phrase did not match what I found. By dusk, the bakery had reopened, two boys were playing beside the tracks, and the cart stood behind the hardware store with one wheel folded under it.

I wrote down the mayor's sentence because everyone else did. I kept the wheel because nobody mentioned it.
